summary:
# Compact notes on the five-book text

Five public-domain texts, separated by "### BOOK n of 5" headings. Book 1 is the only one whose opening is the Mayor's murder; each book's characters and plot are separate.

---

## BOOK 1 of 5: *In the Mayor's Parlour* (J. S. Fletcher, 1922, Gutenberg 25424)

**Setting:** Hathelsborough, an ancient English borough. Market-place with High Cross and Low Cross; St. Hathelswide church (Virgin and Martyr); Moot Hall (ancient, with iron gates, curfew rung 60 min after sunset); Castle keep; streets River Gate, Meadow Gate, Barley Market, St. Laurence Lane, Abbey Gate, Farthing Lane. Taverns: the *Chancellor* Hotel, Bull's Snug (sawdust, skylight, tavern near High Cross). Newspaper: the *Monitor* (editor-reporter Peppermore).

**Characters:**
- John Wallingford: Mayor, 41, reformer, solicitor, "480th" Mayor, elected by one vote. Found stabbed from behind across his desk in the Mayor's Parlour, April evening.
- Richard (Dick) Brent: London journalist, Wallingford's cousin and sole heir (~£15,000). Later stands for Castle Ward Council seat (loses), buys Acacia Lodge (£2,000 guineas) from Chillingham, marries/relationship hinted; ends with Queenie.
- Bunning: ex-sergeant-major, caretaker of Moot Hall; wife (Mrs. Bunning, fetches supper beer at Chancellor Vaults).
- Spizey (Stephen): Bellman, Town Crier, Mace-Bearer; wife Sarah Jane Spizey (huge charwoman, cleans Moot Hall).
- Hawthwaite: borough police superintendent. Hires a London detective; brings in the rapier and typewriter.
- Dr. Wellesley: police surgeon, rival of Wallingford over Mrs. Saumarez; Councillor, Reform man. Assistant Dr. Rutherford Carstairs (Scot). Dr. Barber.
- Simon Crood: Alderman, tanner, Deputy-Mayor, one of three Town Trustees; later elected Mayor. Niece Queenie Crood (orphan, wants stage career). House: Tannery House.
- Krevin Crood: Simon's ne'er-do-well brother, ex-Town Clerk/Magistrates' Clerk, pensioned £156/yr (actually £300). Confesses at the trial; the murderer is Mrs. Saumarez.
- Mallett (bank manager, Town Trustee; wife Mrs. Mallett, who visited Wellesley and Wallingford the evening of murder; leaves him when she discovers affair with Mrs. Saumarez); Coppinger (borough treasurer, Trustee).
- Anita Saumarez: pretty widow, Abbey House, companion Mrs. Elstrick; former flirt of Wellesley and Wallingford; was the one who stabbed Wallingford with the Spanish rapier.
- Epplewhite (Samuel John): Reform party man, tradesman; produced the anonymous threatening letter (typed on Simon Crood's typewriter).
- Tansley: solicitor; Coroner Seagrave; Meeking (police barrister); Cotman (Wellesley's solicitor); Stedman (Simon's solicitor).
- Louisa Speck: Mallett's parlour-maid, supplies handkerchief evidence.
- Peppermore (editor), boy Jimmy Pryder (assistant).
- Owthwaite (Samuel): mechanic who traced typewriter. Nettleton: borough accountant who resigned. Dr. Pellery: antiquary revealing secret passage through St. Lawrence tower / connecting wall to Moot Hall Mayor's Parlour panel.
- Mrs. Marriner: laundry proprietor; identified Wellesley's handkerchief.
- Winifred Wilson: Wellesley's housemaid. Mrs. Appleyard: Wallingford's landlady.

**Plot in order:** Wallingford stabbed while Bunning (who saw him enter at ~7:25) and Brent (arriving ~8) find him. Half-burnt blood-stained cambric handkerchief from hearth. Brent suspects political murder; Crood, Mallett, Coppinger deny. Rapier found behind bookcase (bought from curiosity shop). Inquest adjourned; Epplewhite produces threatening typewritten letter. Wallingford's will (made a week before death) leaves all to Brent. Brent buys Acacia Lodge, stands for council, publishes attack in *Monitor*. Krevin arrested along with Simon; Mallett and Coppinger flee. Krevin confesses at magistrates' court: Mrs. Saumarez struck Wallingford after Krevin heard their quarrel through the secret panel; Krevin wiped hand on Mallett's handkerchief and burned it. Brent rushes to Mrs. Saumarez's house; she has fled with Mallett (telegram "Lingmore Cross Roads six-thirty"). Last chapter: Brent and Queenie in summer-house.

**Ending:** Brent wins Queenie; Peppermore, Tansley recurring. Appendix lists "New Fiction" from John Lane publisher.

---

## BOOK 2 of 5: *Jimmy Quixote* (Tom Gallon, 1906, Gutenberg 41754)

**Book I:** Old Paul (Paul Nannock), rich, shy, heartbroken hermit at Daisley Place, Daisley Cross. Brings home shopping from London. Companions: Patience (old servant, hard-faced, loves Paul); Anthony Ditchburn (wheezing, cultured, parasitic scholar who came in a storm, smokes Paul's tobacco); the "babies": Moira (dark-eyed, Paul's dead lover's child, Paul's chief love), Jimmy Larrance (orphan boy, Quixote), Alice Vickery (fair, pretty, prim; mother flighty). Rector Rev. Temple Purdue teaches the children; his son Charlie Purdue (wild). Baffalls (Mr. Daniel and Mrs. Flora Baffall, retired London trades; Alice visits them). Honora Jackman: flirtatious, eyeglass, sets her eye on Paul; seduces Jimmy into revealing their secret wood; Paul tells Jimmy "Jimmy Quixote". Elopement with donkey "the Ancient One" and chaise. Anthony tells Honora they eloped. Old Paul dies suddenly, having written in the night; Mr. Matthew Shandler (a cousin) claims the estate. Children dispersed: Alice to Baffalls, Jimmy to London warehouse (Baffall recommendation), Moira to London with Patience (Chelsea, Locker Street). Moira's letter to Alice; she visits Mr. Baffall's rooms; Jimmy at warehouse; Anthony wanders.

**Book II:** Jimmy at Camden Town boarding-house, becomes writer, sold stories to a paper; editor (flaxen-haired), boy William. Rooms off Holborn. Writes novel; Mr. Bennett Godsby (actor) turns it into a play, paid. Charlie Purdue dismissed; Moira visits Jimmy and offers breakfast; Charlie proposes to Moira; Charlie seduces Moira (night, opera-going); Moira pregnant. Jimmy learns (Charlie dies, hit in an accident, asks Jimmy to marry Moira). Jimmy weds Moira (dull wedding), she refuses his tenderness.
   - Actually: Charlie tells Jimmy on deathbed; Jimmy promises to marry her; wedding.

**Book III:** Jimmy fancies Alice (Baffalls), who is courted by Ashby Feak; Jimmy hints of a secret marriage; then Moira comes to Jimmy's room; he tells Moira there is someone else (Alice). Anthony Ditchburn steals Moira's letters (written to Jimmy, never sent) and gives them to Jimmy; Jimmy reads them and realises Moira loved him; Moira gone; Patience: Jimmy takes baby girl Moira, finds Moira at Paul's grave/Daisley; reconciliation: "Love had shown them the way."

Final: "THE END."

---

## BOOK 3 of 5: *Tinman* (Tom Gallon, 1907, Gutenberg 48989)

**Part I:** Narrator Charles Avaline (later "Tinman"), guardian Jervis Fanshawe (manager of Patton & Co., London, City office; crafty, gambler indebted to Gavin Hockley). Hockley (bully, drinks, blackmailer) at dinner party in Bloomsbury house. Hammerstone Market: Avaline sees Barbara Patton (daughter of old Patton, wood-meeting; they fall in love). Hockley lies on grass; Fanshawe seen by pond; Avaline's easel ruined by Hockley's heel. Patton dinner: Barbara engaged to cousin Lucas Savell (announced). Avaline strikes Hockley on terrace when Hockley drags Barbara; Hockley slandering Barbara. Barbara's note "Prince Charlie" (signed BARBARA). Card-game losses (~£30 then ~£70 owed to Hockley); Fanshawe pays nothing, says Avaline owes. Night of supper at Hammerstone inn: Avaline attacks Hockley when he says Barbara "had many loves." Avaline goes to Hockley's rooms in Lincoln's Inn Fields; kills him with a sword (Hockley had withheld a cheque). Arrested; tried (Fanshawe testifies); found guilty, death sentence, commuted to penal servitude for life on account of youth. Twenty years in prison (No. 145). Barbara dies at sea (in fiction; in truth alive, escapes husband via stewardess). Freed; picked up outside prison gates by Fanshawe.

**Part II:** Fanshawe takes Avaline to his room (Moggs, the girl; Felix? no). Fanshawe's accomplice Murray Olivant (wealthy, cruel). Olivant names him "Tinman". Olivant plans to marry Barbara Savell (daughter of Barbara). Hammerstone Market house: Lucas Savell (drunk). Barbara Savell (daughter, 'new Barbara'). Arnold Millard (Olivant's half-brother; loves Barbara Savell). Dawkins (smiling henchman). Olivant tries to kidnap; Tinman frees himself; Olivant killed by someone (Arnold? Fanshawe? Confessed: Fanshawe killed Olivant in Lincoln's Inn Fields; Tinman misled). Lucas Savell has a stroke. The elder Barbara (Barbara, the original, alive as "Barbara Avaline"/Mrs. Savell in disguise) reunites with Charlie. Final: Charlie (Tinman) marries Barbara; he has "Charles Avaline's" name; they live a quiet life. Fanshawe dies on the sea voyage (SS Eaglet wreck).

Key objects: tinman's trade/prison numeral "145"; the rapier; the sailor-knife; steamer tickets for Eaglet.

## BOOK 4 of 5: *Won at Last; or, Mrs. Briscoe's Nephews* (Agnes Giberne)

**Family:** Robert Hazel (clerk, London mercantile firm Peterson & Co.), wife Marion (narrator). Children: Jack (eldest, slow, loving, later marries Maimie), Cherry (twin, sensible, loving), Cresswell "Cress" (twin, clever, selfish, handsome, goes to India), Owen (steady, sent to north of England), Frederick "Fred" (training ship), Bob (Robert), Edmund "Ted" (youngest, fair-haired). Nine total.

**Maimie Browne (Mary):** stepdaughter of Churton Hazel (Robert's brother, wild, Canada/US), arrives unannounced; her mother was Mrs. Browne (deceased). Lovely, flaxen hair, black eyes, independent. Churton sent her home without letter; she falls ill (inflammation), nursed by Marion/Cherry. Aunt Briscoe (Mrs. Elizabeth Briscoe, Robert's aunt by marriage; "The Gables"; rheumatic; husband's money); Maimie teaches the younger boys; Jack and Cress both love her; Cress strikes Jack; Maimie's arm bruised; Cress leaves for India. Jack's Bushey Park confession. Churton's plot: he tries to take Maimie; she confronts him: she goes to The Gables; Aunt Briscoe's will: first leaves all to Robert; codicil to Churton (dated 3 weeks before death); last codicil reverts to Robert, £1,000 to Jack, £500 to Robert (Maimie's doing). Churton leaves; Jack and Maimie engaged; married after three years.

Other: Mr. Morison (Jack's employer); Mr. Wilson (lawyer).

---

## BOOK 5 of 5: *The Runaways* (Nat Gould)

**Hazelwell** (Redmond Maynard, Squire, hunting man; wolf-hound Bersak; son Ulick Maynard). Ulick accused (two years earlier, the night he left home) of seducing Janet Todd, daughter of Eli Todd (stud manager). Janet ran off with Warren Courtly (Irene's husband) and was hidden at Mrs. Hoffman's house, Feltham, as "Mrs. Warren". Irene Carstone (Squire's ward; daughter of Colonel Carstone), married Warren Courtly of Anselm Manor. Horse Random (bay hunter, painted by Irene; Ulick's former horse). Honeysuckle (old mare; foal born 1 Jan at midnight; Ulick saw). The Saint: grey colt (by Father Confessor out of Hilda), bought by Ulick via Fred May (trainer) for 200 guineas; rider Ben Sprig; wins Pastures Handicap at Kempton, Coronation Cup at Epsom (beats Vulture). Felix Hoffman: blackmailing begging-letter writer; sent letter to Irene; Warren pays him.

Events: Irene visits Janet; learns truth (Warren was the man). Squire and Ulick reconcile at Newmarket (plot by Eli and Fred May). Warren sold Holme Farm (£10,000). Warren dies in fall jumping Glen church wall while hunting (Rushshire hounds; Ulick riding Random). Janet returns to Eli. Ulick proposes to Irene; married; Irene's son born.
